finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches a caller-supplied URL. The only check is `urlparse(url).hostname.endswith("example.com")`. It has no leading dot, so it also accepts attacker-registered domains such as `evilexample.com` or `example.com.attacker.net`. This is not the same as the defined `ALLOWED_SUFFIX = ".example.com"`, which is never used. The scheme is not restricted. The check runs on the hostname string before DNS resolution, so a name that resolves to a private IP also passes. The attacker controls DNS and can point `x.evilexample.com` at 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1 or an internal service, or use a rebinding record. The check parses with urllib and the fetch parses with httpx, which is a validator/fetcher parser mismatch that lets crafted URLs diverge. The response body is not returned, only `len(r.text)`, so this is a semi-blind SSRF. The length and the status-dependent behaviour are still an oracle for internal probing, and a 5xx raised by the fetch can also leak information.
finding.source: `url` query parameter of GET /mirror (FastAPI), fully attacker-controlled

trace.note: `url: str` is read directly from the query string
urlparse(url).hostname is extracted for validation, using a different parser from the one httpx uses to fetch
Check is `host.endswith("example.com")`. It has no dot boundary, it is a string suffix check, not an allowlist of resolved IPs, and it does not check the scheme or port
The original, unmodified `url` string is passed to httpx `c.get(url)`. The URL is not rebuilt from parsed components and no DNS pinning is done

finding.guards_checked: Hostname suffix check without a leading dot (bypassable with `evilexample.com`, `attacker-example.com`, or any registrant-controlled name ending in example.com). The `ALLOWED_SUFFIX` constant is unused. There is no scheme check, no resolved-IP/private-range check, no DNS pinning, and no egress filtering in the code. httpx does not follow redirects by default, so redirect-based bypass is not a factor. /ping at mirror.py:23 uses a hardcoded URL and is not vulnerable.

verdict.guard_found: Only `host.endswith("example.com")` at mirror.py:13, a suffix check with no leading dot. The `ALLOWED_SUFFIX` constant at line 7 is unused. There is no scheme check, no IP check, and no auth or middleware in the file.
verdict.reason: The caller-controlled `url` (mirror.py:11) passes only the bypassable `endswith("example.com")` check (mirror.py:13), so `evilexample.com` reaches `c.get(url)` at mirror.py:16 and the SSRF is real, though semi-blind because only `len(r.text)` is returned at line 17.
